# A US vendor's bill for one litre of fuel, expensed to an account kept to
# thousandths.
#
# Fuel is priced to a tenth of a cent — 1.819 a litre — so the expense account
# is denominated at 1/1000 rather than at the cent, which GnuCash keeps per
# account and this tool round-trips as `commodity_scu:`. One litre is 1.819
# CAD: an amount the currency cannot hold and the account can, which is the
# whole reason such accounts exist (see account_with_finer_scu.txt). On an
# ordinary CAD account the same figure is refused.
#
# The bill is in USD, so the payable credit is a cost basis priced through
# that CAD split. Applying the transaction's rate back to it has to round the
# way the split itself is held — to the thousandth — or the implied figure is
# 1.82 against a carried 1.819 and a correct book reads as converted at two
# rates, over a difference smaller than the cent the message would print both
# figures at.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_verify_costs.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses:Fuel
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
	commodity_scu: 1000
2026-01-01 open Liabilities
	type: Liability
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD
	type: Accounts Payable
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"

2026-01-10 * "One litre of fuel from a US vendor, at 1.399 CAD/USD"
	currency.mnemonic: "USD"
	Expenses:Fuel 1.819 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		value: "1.30"
	Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD -1.30 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		value: "-1.30"
